edit.description: `BudgetReading` names the declared window and the prior turn's tokens; each fraction is computed from them rather than stored beside them
the crossing reads the computed fraction, and the arm for a windowed reading carrying none goes
the case driving a windowed budget over a fraction-less reading
the windowed and windowless reads, on the shape they compose

summary: The budget reading stores a fraction beside no window, so `budgetLineDue` holds an arm for a windowed reading carrying none — a state the type permits and no read composes

per.section: Derived state is computed, never restated beside its source

acceptance: the reading names the window and the tokens its fractions are taken over, the fractions are computed where they are compared, and no arm answers for a windowed reading that carries none
notes: Per note A-DECLARED-THRESHOLD-NEEDS-THE-WINDOW-IT-CROSSES, item 2, verified this drain: thresholds now need a window (`validateBudget`), so `src/budgetHook.ts:248` answers only for a reading `readBudgetLine` cannot compose and `tests/budgetHook.test.ts:206` drives exactly that. `src/budgetLine.ts:190` re-checks window and fraction where one implies the other. Behavior-free — same line, same crossings. Claims no property; tsc and the two budget suites hold it.
